subject: general
question: The rotors in a roots air-blower type supercharger are designed in which geometric shape?
solution:
The correct answer is __Epicycloid shape.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Roots air-blower type superchargers__ are used to increase engine air intake efficiency.
 
• The rotors in these superchargers are designed in epicycloid shape to ensure efficient airflow and proper sealing.
 
• The epicycloid shape helps maintain uniform pressure in the blower.
 
• It minimizes air leakage and ensures consistent delivery of compressed air to the engine.
 
• This design is crucial for high-performance engines where precise air intake is essential.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Spiral Shape:**

 
 
• Used in other components like turbochargers or fans, but not in roots air-blowers.
 
• Spiral shapes are designed for specific airflow dynamics.
 
 
 
• **Cylindrical Shape:**
 
 
• Cylindrical designs are common in pistons and certain valves.
 
• They are not effective for the rotor design in roots air-blowers.
 
 
 
• **Helical Shape:**
 
 
• Helical shapes are used in screw compressors, not roots blowers.
 
• They provide continuous and smooth compression, unlike epicycloid shapes.
